channel.description: This is a randomly ordered feed of the most recent entries from summarizedStoriesMainNLscienceAndDiscovery, skipping any feeds with errors.

item.title: Popular sweeteners may have multigenerational effects
item.description: Sucralose and stevia, common zero-calorie sweeteners, may produce effects that persist across generations, according to mouse studies.

item.title: Scientists debunk 70-year-old 'lizard brain' theory
item.description: The idea of a primitive 'lizard brain' beneath newer rational layers is likely flawed, according to researchers challenging traditional views of brain evolution.

item.title: Researchers find two distinct superconducting states in one material
item.description: New research reveals that two ultrathin superconductors, including niobium diselenide, have more complex behavior than previously thought, with hidden dual states.

item.title: Monkey foot flexibility could challenge human evolution theories
item.description: West African monkeys can climb vertical trunks using foot flexibility that was previously unknown, raising questions about how fossilized feet are interpreted.
